title: Rollout decider signal cookbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-first cookbook for the final 14-day ramp and first 72h post-rollout. Goal: give on-call, product ops, and ENG a short set of signal definitions + binary decision rules to (a) proceed, (b) pause/rollback, or (c) continue with mitigations.

Scope:
- Applies to feature rollouts that touch the hosted API, Dedicated capacity routing, or routing policies (routing changes, model variant fallbacks, or batching defaults).
- Not for infra-only maintenance (SRE runbooks still apply).

High-level signal categories (radio metaphor):
- Heartbeat (service health): 5xx rate, pod restarts, infra CPU/GPU saturation
- Experience (user-facing): median latency P50/P95, streaming stalls, token dropouts
- Quality (model output): hallucination/failure rate from eval prompts, customer complaints
- Economics (cost): cost per 1k tokens, unexpected quota burn, cache miss rate
- Adoption (traffic): request growth, new client cohorts, throttling events

Signal dictionary (compact):
- 5xx-rate: percentage of requests returning 5xx over rolling 5m window. Thresholds: green <0.1%, amber 0.1-0.5%, red >0.5%. Owner: SRE.
- infra-gpu-util: GPU utilization cluster-level 5m avg. Thresholds: green <78%, amber 78-92%, red >92%. Owner: Infra Eng.
- p95-latency-ms: end-to-end request P95. Thresholds: green <350ms, amber 350-700ms, red >700ms. Owner: Product-API.
- stream-drop-rate: percent of streaming sessions that disconnect or produce empty chunks. Green <0.3%, amber 0.3-1%, red >1%. Owner: Serving Runtime.
- model-regression-score: automated eval on golden prompts, delta vs baseline (lower is worse). Thresholds: green delta >= -0.5 pts, amber -0.5 to -1.5, red < -1.5. Owner: Applied ML.
- token-cost-burn: observed cost per 1k tokens vs projection. Amber if >20% above projection; red if >50% above. Owner: Finance/Platform.
- cache-miss-rate: end-to-end prefix/KV cache miss %. Amber >25%, red >45%. Owner: Serving Runtime.

Decision rules (short binary heuristics):
1) Go / No-Go for progressive ramp (day N -> N+1):
   - Green: All Heartbeat + Experience signals green for 30m post-step, model-regression-score not amber/red, economics within +/-20%. Proceed.
   - Amber: Any single amber + no reds and owners have mitigation queued and estimated <60m to reduce. Proceed with hold (pause new cohort, keep existing). Notify product-ops.
   - Red: Any red in Heartbeat or Experience OR model-regression red -> STOP, rollback to previous variant or divert to fallback model, page SRE + Applied ML.

2) Immediate rollback (hard rule):
   - If 5xx-rate red OR infra-gpu-util red AND trending upwards for 10m -> immediate rollback (automated or manual per ops).
   - If model-regression-score red AND customer-visible hallucinations > 2% AND top-tier customers affected -> rollback and launch customer notify.

Owner radio roster (who does what in the first 60 minutes after a red):
- Pager 1 (SRE): verify 5xx logs, check autoscaler, revert infra changes, escalate to infra lead.
- Pager 2 (Serving Runtime): check batching queue length, KV cache status, hot-shard mapping.
- Applied ML lead: run quick eval suite on staging golden prompts, validate model weights/quantization artifacts.
- Product-ops (owner): coordinate stakeholder comms, run decision template, update status channel.
- Support lead: triage incoming customer messages, label with 'launch-incident' tag.

Mitigation playbook (quick steps):
- Heartbeat red: reduce traffic on new variant -> switch routing to baseline variant, scale up headroom nodes, temporarily disable batching heuristics introduced in this rollout.
- Latency amber->red: enable emergency per-request async response paths (if implemented), reduce batch sizes to lower p95, route heavy customers to dedicated pools.
- Model-quality red: revert to prior model checkpoint, disable experimental prompts/enrichers, open a hotfix PR for model config.
- Cost surge: throttle non-critical endpoints, enable higher batching and caching, notify finance and product for temporary quota top-ups.

Canary & phased cadence (example 14-day):
- Day -14 to -7: internal alpha, non-prod smoke. Run synthetic load: 10k synthetic requests/day; collect baseline signals.
- Day -7 to -3: seeded beta with 2% traffic (internal + trusted customers). Observe 24/7. Decision checkpoint at day -3.
- Day -2: expand to 10% traffic (mixed cohorts). Two full technical reviews: infra & ML.
- Day 0: 25% -> 50% over 3 hours if green. Hold 2 hours at each step.
- Day 1-7: incremental ramp to 100%, daily telemetry digest and customer feedback check-in.
- Day 7-14: observation window, reduce monitoring sampling for long-tail metrics but keep golden evals active.

Quick checklist (pre-roll):
- Owners assigned and reachable (list + offsets)
- Synthetic golden prompt suite run and stored (link in linked_artifacts)
- Emergency rollback path smoke-tested (manual and automated)
- Capacity buffer (20% private, 30% hosted) reserved for first 72h
- Support runbook seeded in shared channel (templates for customer comms)

Simulation steps (recommended short rehearsal):
- T-72h: tabletop exercise: simulate 5xx spike + model-regression amber; walk decision tree, record time-to-decision and action.
- T-36h: run automated failover drill (traffic switch to baseline) in staging with production-like data.
- T-1h: small blast traffic to ensure autoscaling triggers behave as expected.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Should we add a separate "contracted-customer-impact" signal that weights customers by SLA? (Priya to propose weighting math)
- Confirm whether Dedicated pools can be used as instant fallbacks for hosted traffic—infra team to confirm network routing time (Ethan).
- Need a short URL for the golden prompt suite results (Lena to add).

Next steps (ownership):
- Product-ops: finalize signal thresholds with SRE & Applied ML by 2024-10-09.
- Applied ML: validate model-regression quick-suite and add one new hallucination prompt by 2024-10-07.
- Infra: confirm fallback routing latency for Dedicated pools by 2024-10-04 and post to this doc.

Appendix (short):
- Decision template (use in incident channel):
  1) Signal(s) triggered + magnitude
  2) Immediate action taken (route/switch/rollback)
  3) Owners paged + ETA for next update
  4) Customer impact estimate (users affected, percent of traffic)
  5) Next steps and time for a full postmortem

This doc is intentionally terse — treat as the radio quick-guide and link back to the longer runbooks in Confluence. Feedback welcome; will iterate after the next dry-run.

-- Morgan (product-ops)
